sheets.title: Satavahanas and the Sangam age (300 BCE – 300 CE)
sheets.intro: Satavahana kings, government, trade, art; Sangam kings, books, society.

keys.name: Sangam age

rows.v: c. 300 BCE – 300 CE
Tamilakam – Tamil Nadu, Kerala
Muvendar (three crowned kings) – Chera, Chola, Pandya; Velir chiefs below
Sangam poems, twin epics; Roman coins; Keeladi, Arikamedu, Adichanallur
Gajabahu synchronism (Senguttuvan and Gajabahu I of Sri Lanka, 2nd c. CE)
Ashoka RE II, XIII (Cholas, Pandyas, Keralaputras, Satiyaputras); Hathigumpha (Tamil confederacy broken); Megasthenes (Pandya land ruled by women); Periplus, Pliny, Ptolemy (Muziris)

traps: Sangam Cholas ≠ imperial Cholas (9th – 13th c.)

rows.v: Madurai; head Agastya; nothing survives (Agattiyam lost)
Kapadapuram; head Tolkappiyar; Tolkappiyam survives
Madurai; head Nakkirar; Ettuthokai and Pattuppattu
Pandyas

keys.name: Satavahanas

rows.v: c. 1st c. BCE (Puranas: 230 BCE) – early 3rd c. CE; Matsya Purana – 30 kings, about 460 years
"Andhras" / "Andhrabhrityas" in the Puranas
Pratishthana (Paithan, Godavari) in the west; Dhanyakataka (Dharanikota, Amaravati, Krishna) in the east
AP, Telangana, Maharashtra, Karnataka, MP
Simuka's coins at Kotilingala (Karimnagar, Telangana) – Telugu land view; others say western Deccan
Bridge between north and south
Brahmin kings (Ashvamedha, Rajasuya) who also gave land to Buddhist monks

traps: Pratishthana is in Maharashtra; Amaravati in AP

keys.name: Simuka

rows.v: c. 60 – 37 BCE (order matters more than year)
Founder; ended Shunga (Kanva) rule in the Deccan
Rathikas, Bhojakas
Naneghat inscription
Brother Kanha (Krishna) – in a Nasik cave inscription

traps: Simuka was followed by his brother Kanha, not his son

keys.name: Satakarni I

rows.v: Third king, after Kanha
Malwa, Narmada valley; clash with Kharavela (Hathigumpha)
Dakshinapathapati (Lord of Dakshinapatha)
Two Ashvamedhas, Rajasuya; huge priest fees
Nayanika (Naganika), daughter of a Maharathi; regent; Naneghat inscription (Pune)
Ananda, artisans' foreman of Siri Satakarni, gave the south gateway

traps: Naneghat (Nayanika, Satakarni I) ≠ Nasik (Gautami Balashri, Gautamiputra)

keys.name: Hala

rows.v: c. 20 – 24 CE; short, peaceful
Gatha Saptasati (Gaha Sattasai) – 700 love verses in Maharashtri Prakrit
Gunadhya – Brihatkatha (Paishachi Prakrit); Sarvavarman – Katantra (Sanskrit grammar)
Matsya Purana

traps: Hala = Gatha Saptasati; Gunadhya = Brihatkatha

keys.name: Gautamiputra Satakarni

rows.v: c. 106 – 130 CE; greatest Satavahana
Beat Nahapana (Kshaharata Shaka) – restruck his coins (Jogalthembi hoard, Nasik); beat Shakas, Pahlavas, Yavanas
Malwa, Saurashtra, Konkan to Vidarbha and the Krishna
Nasik Prashasti by mother Gautami Balashri (19th year of Pulumavi)
Ekabrahmana; Kshatriya-darpa-mana-mardana; Shaka-Yavana-Pahlava-nisudana; Trisamudra-toya-pita-vahana (horses drank 3 seas); Benakataka-svami
Stopped mixing of the four varnas; also gave land to Buddhist monks

traps: Gautamiputra beat Nahapana; Rudradaman marriage is Pulumavi’s

rows.v: c. 130 – 154 CE; son of Gautamiputra
To the Krishna mouth; inscriptions at Amaravati
Navanagara-svami (lord of the new city)
Ship motifs (sea trade)
Married Rudradaman I's daughter (Junagadh); Rudradaman beat "Satakarni" twice but spared him
c. 165 – 194 CE; last great king
Won back Malwa, Konkan from the Shakas
Ship coins
Inscription at Chinna Ganjam (Prakasam)
Weak kings; feudatories broke away

keys.name: Women and matronymics

rows.v: Named after mother – Gautami-putra, Vasishthi-putra
Queen-regent for a minor son
Had the Nasik Prashasti carved
Varna order; merchants and artisans rose; women fairly high status

traps: Matronymic = from the mother, not the father

keys.name: Satavahana government

rows.v: Janapada → Rashtra → Ahara (district, under Amatyas) → Vishaya → Grama
Rajas (highest; minted coins) > Mahabhojas (Thane – Kolaba) > Maharathis (Poona)
Gramani; Gaulmika (military)
9 chariots, 9 elephants, 25 horses, 45 foot soldiers
Senapati (also governor); Rajjuka (revenue); Bhandagarika (treasurer); Paniyagharika (waterworks); Karmantika (works); Avesanika (artisans' foreman)
"Rajan"; council of Raja-Amatyas; decentralised, feudal

traps: Only Rajas among feudatories minted coins

keys.name: Satavahana economy

rows.v: Krishna – Godavari rice; paddy transplanting
Uttarapatha, Dakshinapatha
Kalyan, Sopara, Bharuch (Barygaza)
Ghantasala, Masulipatnam (Maisolos), Ganjam
Mostly lead; also copper, bronze, potin; silver portrait coins (Shaka style); Prakrit in Brahmi; ship, chaitya, animal designs
Shrenis – weavers, oil pressers, potters; rich gifts to caves
Trade via Barygaza (Periplus, Ptolemy)
First tax-free grants to Brahmins (agraharas) and monks – seed of feudalism

traps: Satavahana coins were mainly lead, not gold
Tamralipti was not a Satavahana port

keys.name: Satavahana art

rows.v: Stupa begun 3rd c. BCE; white limestone reliefs, Jatakas; found by Colin Mackenzie (first Surveyor General)
Karle (largest chaitya; Yavana donors); Bhaja; Nasik (Pandavleni); Kanheri; Junnar
Caves 9, 10 (early)
Prakrit at court

traps: Ajanta 9, 10 = Satavahana; 1, 2, 16, 17, 26 = Vakataka

keys.name: After the Satavahanas

rows.v: Ikshvakus (Nagarjunakonda)
Abhiras, Chutus
Pallavas
Weak heirs; feudatories broke away

traps: In Andhra the successors were the Ikshvakus, not the Pallavas

rows.v: Bow (Villavar); Vanji (Karur); ports Muziris, Tondi; Kerala, west TN
Tiger; Uraiyur (cotton); port Puhar (Kaveripattinam); Cauvery delta to S Andhra (Pennar – Vellar); titles Senni, Valavan, Killi
Fish; Madurai (Vaigai); port Korkai (pearls); titles Thennavar, Minavar
Early Sangam Chola
Ruled in Sri Lanka; praised for justice (Mahavamsa)
Beaten by Sinhala prince Dutugemunu

keys.name: Karikala Chola

rows.v: After family fights over the throne
Beat Chera, Pandya and 11 chiefs
Beat 9 chiefs
Grand Anicut on the Cauvery – among the oldest working dams
Roman, Greek trade hub (Pattinappalai)

traps: Kallanai is Sangam Chola work, not imperial Chola

keys.name: Chera kings

rows.v: Perumchotru Udhiyan Cheralathan; fed both Mahabharata armies (legend) – a Chera, not Chola (UPSC 2026)
Himalayan expedition (Pathitrupathu)
Himalayan raid; founded Pattini (Kannagi) cult; Gajabahu attended – dating anchor
Pepper to Rome; temple of Augustus at Muziris (Peutinger Table)

traps: Only Senguttuvan is linked to Kannagi and Gajabahu

keys.name: Pandya kings

rows.v: Wrongly executed Kovalan → Kannagi burnt Madurai
Won Thalaiyalanganam vs Chera – Chola – Velir
Last Sangam Pandya; then the Kalabhras
Envoys to the Pandya court

traps: Two different Neduncheliyans

keys.name: Sangam literature

rows.v: Tolkappiyar – oldest Tamil grammar; also society, economy
8 anthologies – Purananuru (puram), Akananuru (akam)
10 idylls – Pattinappalai (Puhar, Karikala); Maduraikanchi (Madurai's day and night markets – Nalangadi, Allangadi); Tirumurugarruppadai (Murugan)
Akam (love, inner) and Puram (war, fame, outer)
18 moral works
Thiruvalluvar; 1,330 couplets – Aram (virtue), Porul (wealth), Inbam (love); "Tamil Veda"
Kapilar, Nakkirar, Avvaiyar

traps: Ettuthokai = eight; Pattuppattu = ten
Tirukkural’s third part is love, not moksha

keys.name: Twin epics

rows.v: Ilango Adigal; "tale of the anklet"; Kannagi and Kovalan; justice; base of the Pattini cult
Sittalai Sattanar; Buddhist; daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi becomes a nun
Also Civaka Cintamani (Jain)

traps: Silappadikaram – Ilango; Manimekalai (Buddhist) – Sattanar

keys.name: Five landscapes (Tinai)
keys.hook: Hills Murugan, pasture Vishnu, farm Indra, coast Varuna, desert Korravai

rows.v: Murugan; hunting, honey; Kuravar, Vetar
Vishnu (Mayon); cattle; Ayar (Idaiyar)
Indra; farming; Vellalar, Uzhavar
Varuna; fishing, salt; Paratavar
Korravai; raiding; Maravar, Eyinar

traps: Marudam = Indra; Neydal = Varuna

rows.v: Arasar (rulers), Anthanar (priests), Vanigar (traders), Vellalar (farmers)
Fairly free; women poets (Avvaiyar); Karpu (chastity) ideal
Murugan (Seyon) – six abodes (Arupadai Veedu); Korravai, Mayon, Indra, Varuna
Nadu Kal for fallen warriors

keys.name: Sangam economy and trade

rows.v: Rice; sugarcane, cotton, pepper, turmeric, ginger, jackfruit (Chera)
Uraiyur cotton; Arikamedu beads, pottery; Madurai jewellery; Kanchipuram textiles
Barter; Umanar (salt traders); Chattu (travelling merchants); Chattan, Nigama (guilds); Vanikan (merchant)
Puhar, Muziris, Korkai, Arikamedu, Tondi
Pepper, spices, cloth, pearls, ivory
Gold, Roman wine, horses
Roman gold, silver coin hoards (worn as ornaments too); Yavanas = Greek, Roman traders

traps: Uraiyur = cotton; Korkai = pearls; Arikamedu = beads, Roman pottery

keys.name: Sangam government

rows.v: Hereditary; Amaichar (ministers), Anthanar, Senathipathi, Otrar (spies), Thuthar (envoys)
Mandalam (province) → Nadu (district) → Ur (town) → Perur / Sirur (big / small village); Pattinam (port), Cheri (suburb)
Karai (land), Ulgu (customs), Irai (tribute), Iravu (extra demand); war booty
Standing; banner Kodimaram

traps: Karai = land; Ulgu = customs; Irai = tribute

rows.v: Vaigai near Madurai; literate town; Tamil-Brahmi sherds; carbon dates c. 6th c. BCE; ASI report row (2025 – 26)
Near Puducherry; Wheeler 1945; Roman Arretine ware, amphorae, beads
Thamirabarani; Iron Age urn burials, bronze, iron

keys.name: Kalabhra "dark age"

rows.v: c. 3rd – 6th century CE
Kalabhras overran Tamil land for 250+ years
Buddhism, Jainism grew
Pallavas and Pandyas, 6th century

traps: Kalabhras ended the Sangam order; Pallavas revived it
